statement: (i) Differentiate $y=x\ln x$ and $y=\ln(x^{2}+1)$. (ii) Find the minimum value of $x\ln x$ for $x>0$. (iii) Evaluate $\int_{1}^{e}\ln x\,dx$.
solution: (i) $\frac{d}{dx}(x\ln x)=\ln x+1$; $\frac{d}{dx}\ln(x^{2}+1)=\frac{2x}{x^{2}+1}$. (ii) Minimum where $\ln x+1=0\Rightarrow x=e^{-1}$; value $(e^{-1})(-1)=-\frac1e$. (iii) Integration by parts: $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-x$. From $1$ to $e$: $(e-e)-(0-1)=1$.
hints: Use the product rule for x ln x.
